clue.text: Slow day on Wall Street, oddly I'm up following governor and Commander-in-Chief around

parts.note: a vali is a provincial governor in the Ottoman Empire

indicators.note: oddly says these letters come out in a strange, rearranged order
around asks for the abbreviation to be turned so it reads the other way

parts.note: CINC is the military abbreviation for a Commander-in-Chief

explanation.surface: A trader reports a quiet day on Wall Street, with a governor and the top general somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges I'M UP into UMPI, and 'around' turns CINC into CNIC. A Valium picnic is US trader slang for a sluggish day on the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Valium is a sedative, so a market day that feels drugged into calm is jokingly called a picnic of it.

clue.text: Mammal, half size in rock cavity — chap nets six

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word inside the cavity word

parts.note: a vug is a small cavity in a rock, often lined with crystals

indicators.note: half takes only the front part of the word for size, its first four letters

parts.note: size can mean quantity, an amount or extent

indicators.note: nets means catches, so the word for chap surrounds the number

parts.note: a bod is British slang for a person or chap
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A zoologist describes finding a mammal in a hollow in the rock, caught by a man in a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' cuts QUANTITY to QUAN. The Vu Quang bovid, also called the saola, is a rare forest ox found in Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: The saola is a rare cattle-like animal discovered in Vietnam in 1992, so it is a mammal.

clue.text: Plant weapon containing uranium

indicators.note: containing means the weapon word holds the chemical symbol inside it

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A botanist warns that a plant has become a weapon laced with radioactive metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a genus of flowering plants that includes lords-and-ladies.

clue.text: Give a hint of giant-killer regularly appearing

indicators.note: regularly appearing picks every second letter of the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to drop a hint about the hero who slew a giant.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters of giant-killer spells the answer. In Chambers, inkle is an old verb meaning to hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkle is a rare old verb for suggesting or hinting, related to inkling.

clue.text: Note restriction arising after type of light inflammation

parts.note: UV stands for ultraviolet light

indicators.note: arising in a down clue means the pieces are read from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: si is another name for te, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a tie is a restriction or constraint

explanation.surface: A doctor notes that patients' activity was restricted after exposure to a particular kind of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' reverses SI + TIE as a whole, giving EITIS after UV.
explanation.definitionFit: Uveitis is a medical condition where the uvea, the middle layer of the eye, becomes swollen and sore.

clue.text: Stale horse mushroom

annotationWithheld.why: 'Stale horse mushroom (5)' for MOREL: the blog calls it a double definition (horse, mushroom), but no sense of 'Stale' fits a morel, so that word has no job I can justify

clue.text: Wild hog feast sounded costly

parts.note: to pig, or pig out, is to feast greedily

indicators.note: sounded means the next word is taken as it is spoken, not as written

parts.note: dear means costly or expensive

explanation.surface: A banquet featuring a wild boar turned out to be very expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: The pig-deer is the babirusa, a wild pig of Indonesia whose tusks grow up through its snout like antlers.
explanation.definitionFit: The babirusa, or pig-deer, is a wild swine of Sulawesi, so it is a kind of hog.

clue.text: Bury pub outside the town's centre

indicators.note: outside means the pub word goes around the other piece

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: centre keeps only the middle of the word for town, dropping its first and last letters

parts.note: a burg is a town, especially an old or walled one

explanation.surface: Someone wants a pub in the town of Bury, just outside the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' cuts BURG to UR. Bury is also a town in Lancashire, which makes the surface read as a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: To inurn is to place ashes in an urn, a way of laying the dead to rest.

clue.text: Wink, curiously tacit during informal end to the day

indicators.note: during puts the jumbled letters inside the informal word for night

parts.note: nite is an informal spelling of night, which ends the day

indicators.note: curiously signals that these letters are jumbled in an odd way

explanation.surface: Someone gives a silent, knowing wink late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' rearranges TACIT into CTITA, which 'during' places inside NITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To nictitate is the technical verb for blinking or winking the eyelids.

clue.text: What comes from copper working catching forgery in office led by fellow

parts.note: chal is a Romany word for a man or fellow
a copy is an imitation, a forgery
an office can be a religious ceremony or rite

explanation.surface: A clerk caught forging documents in the office was led away by a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces sit side by side in answer order: 'led by fellow' puts CHAL first, and COPY comes before RITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper pyrites is the main ore mined for copper, so it is what copper workings produce.

clue.text: Deportation of children voided in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grim report of children being expelled from a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Renvoi is a legal term for sending a foreigner back out of a country, i.e. expulsion.

clue.text: Keep quiet about "at home" function

indicators.note: about means the hushing word goes round the other piece

parts.note: sh is the sound used to tell someone to keep quiet
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep quiet about a party held at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinh is the hyperbolic sine, a mathematical function.

clue.text: Intellectual activity is one's bent

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thinker says intellectual pursuit is their natural inclination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' rearranges the letters of IS ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Noesis is the philosophical term for pure thought or the working of the intellect.

clue.text: Question kinetic energy in short dispute with new cannon not working

indicators.note: in puts the energy abbreviation inside the shortened dispute word
short cuts the last letter off the word for dispute

parts.note: to argue is to dispute
KE is the physics abbreviation for kinetic energy

explanation.surface: Physicists bicker over kinetic energy, while a new cannon fails to fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims ARGUE to ARGU, and 'in' puts KE inside it to make AKERGU. A Quaker gun is a dummy cannon, named after the pacifist Quakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Quaker gun is a fake piece of artillery, often a painted log, used to deceive the enemy.

clue.text: Fruit syrup layman is confused about

indicators.note: about means the mixed letters go round the syrup word
is confused tells us these letters are mixed up

parts.note: rob is a thick fruit syrup

explanation.surface: An ordinary person is puzzled by fruit syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is confused' rearranges LAYMAN into MYALAN, and 'about' puts it round ROB.
explanation.definitionFit: The myrobalan is a plum-like fruit, also called the cherry plum.

clue.text: Honey badger beginning to ransack a mound

indicators.note: beginning to takes just the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a tel is an ancient mound in the Middle East, built up from earlier settlements

explanation.surface: A honey badger starts raiding an earth mound.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel is another name for the honey badger, a fierce African and Asian mammal.

clue.text: Adult group keeping unknown until now

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult

indicators.note: keeping means the group word holds the unknown inside

parts.note: a set is a group
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A group of grown-ups has kept something unknown so far.
explanation.definitionFit: As yet and until now both mean up to the present time.

clue.text: A source of gum clients chewed

indicators.note: chewed means mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Customers are chewing gum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed' rearranges CLIENTS. The lentisc is the mastic tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The lentisc, or mastic tree, yields mastic, a resin used as a gum.

clue.text: Realign fluid pipe

indicators.note: fluid means not fixed, so the letters can flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A plumber is told to realign a pipe carrying liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluid' rearranges REALIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nargile is a hookah, a water-cooled smoking pipe.

clue.text: Warning a wall's being erected

indicators.note: being erected in a down clue means the word is built from the bottom up, so read backwards

parts.note: mural means of or on a wall

explanation.surface: A warning is issued that a wall is being put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being erected' reverses MURAL into LARUM.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarum is an old word for an alarm or call to arms.

clue.text: Elizabeth keeping look, English dress flashily

indicators.note: keeping means the name holds the other word inside

parts.note: Liz is a short form of Elizabeth
an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: Elizabeth has a showy English look and dresses to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: Lairize is Australian slang for showing off in loud clothes, from lair meaning a flashy dresser.

clue.text: Planned activities time in old courtyard

parts.note: PAT stands for planned activities time, school jargon for structured sessions
I is a short form of in

explanation.surface: A timetable puts organised activities in the old courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: PAT is an abbreviation for planned activities time, a period set aside for organised sessions in a school timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved open area next to a house, originally a Spanish inner courtyard.

clue.text: Instrument the man's removed from Caribbean island, one taken north?

indicators.note: taken north in a down clue means moved higher up, so earlier in the word
removed from means the possessive pronoun is deleted from the island name

parts.note: Hispaniola is the island shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic
his means belonging to the man
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A musician's instrument is carried off a Caribbean island and shipped north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' drops HIS to leave PANIOLA, then 'taken north' moves the I up one place.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianola is a self-playing piano driven by perforated paper rolls.

clue.text: Explain away German defeat

parts.note: a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: Someone tries to talk their way out of a German defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To gloss over or gloss is to give a misleading interpretation that makes something seem acceptable.

clue.text: I am in a file of people battling griffins?

indicators.note: in puts the contracted pronoun phrase inside the file phrase

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file, with the article giving A
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: A soldier says they are in a column of troops fighting mythical beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Arimaspians were a legendary one-eyed people of Scythia, said by Herodotus to steal gold guarded by griffins.
explanation.definitionFit: Arimasp is the name of a member of a mythical one-eyed tribe forever fighting gold-guarding griffins.

clue.text: Parasite, one they locally found on young children

parts.note: babes are babies or young children
I is the Roman numeral one
a is a dialect form of they

explanation.surface: A parasite was found on babies in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found on' puts BABES before the other letters. A is a dialect word for they.
explanation.definitionFit: Babesia is a protozoan blood parasite carried by ticks.

clue.text: Shallow sandy head of a lake primarily

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone describes a sandy spot at the top of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoal is a shallow place in water, and as an adjective it means not deep.

clue.text: Excited taking part in stampede

indicators.note: taking part in means the answer is part of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Excited animals join a stampede.
explanation.definitionFit: Amped is slang for thrilled or worked up.

clue.text: Arranged play and training initially so as to be fit?

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order
initially takes only the first letter of training

explanation.surface: An organised programme of games and exercise is meant to get people fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' rearranges PLAY together with T, the first letter of training. The question mark marks the play on fit meaning suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptly means in a suitable or fitting way, so it describes doing something to fit the case.

clue.text: Pony struggling with large artificial leg

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A pony struggles with a large prosthetic leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges PONY together with L. Chambers gives pylon as slang for an artificial leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Pylon is an old informal name for a simple prosthetic limb fitted below the knee.

clue.text: Something like spinach or pine yielding drug

indicators.note: yielding means giving up the drug letter from the word for pine

parts.note: to ache for something is to pine for it
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Either spinach or pine needles may produce a medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yielding' drops E from ACHE, leaving ACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Orach is a leafy garden plant eaten as a vegetable in the same way as its relative, spinach.

clue.text: Excellent programming language, not British

indicators.note: not means the British abbreviation is left out of the language name

parts.note: COBOL is an old business programming language

explanation.surface: A programmer praises a computer language that isn't British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes B from COBOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool is informal praise meaning great or very good.

clue.text: The masses hold one ballot round India

parts.note: ho is an old call meaning stop or hold
I is the Roman numeral one
a poll is a ballot or vote
O is round in shape
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Ordinary people hold a vote across India.
explanation.walkthrough: Ho is an old exclamation meaning stop, like the command hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi is Greek for the many, used in English for the common people.

clue.text: Way of presenting film orgasm shunned by Sri Lanka

indicators.note: shunned by means the country's code is cut out of the other word

parts.note: a climax is an orgasm
CL is the international vehicle code for Sri Lanka

explanation.surface: A racy scene is cut from a film by Sri Lankan censors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shunned by' removes CL from CLIMAX.
explanation.definitionFit: IMAX is a large-screen cinema format used to show films.

clue.text: Cross about single being knocked back with some spirit

indicators.note: about means the cross word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a zo is a cross between a yak and a cow

indicators.note: being knocked back means the word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: sole means single or only

explanation.surface: An angry person, single and drinking, knocks back some spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being knocked back' reverses SOLE into ELOS, and 'about' puts ZO round it. Zeloso is a musical direction meaning play zealously.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeloso is an Italian musical direction asking for a passage to be played zealously and with energy.

clue.text: Thump once preceded fish moving to and fro

parts.note: ding is an old word for to thump or strike
led means went in front of, preceded
to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: A fish was struck before it swung back and forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingle-dangle means swinging or dangling loosely back and forth.
